hook.text: Fly over Kansas and you'll see green circles from the air—each one a center pivot irrigation system.

buildup.text: A long pipe on wheels rotates around a central well, spraying water in a quarter-mile circle.

discovery.text: Center pivots turned the semi-arid Great Plains into one of the world's most productive farming regions.

twist.text: Most pivots pump from the Ogallala Aquifer, which is being drained far faster than rainfall recharges it.

climax.text: When the aquifer runs dry—projected in parts within decades—those green circles will turn brown.

punchline.text: The circles are green today. The water won't last forever.

quiz.question: Why are center pivot irrigation fields circular?
options: The pipe rotates around a central well, naturally creating a circle
